_comment: Ratchet config for scripts/codecharta-ratchet.py, run against the CodeCharta map (build/habitatus.cc.json.gz). Three gates: (1) per-file aggregate complexity, (2) per-FUNCTION complexity (not gameable by moving code between files), (3) hotspot (complex AND under-tested). Ratchet by LOWERING the numbers as the code improves; RAISING a baseline entry needs a justification in the PR.

complexity._default_cap_note: Per-file SUM of function complexity. Highest non-baseline file is classify.go at 44.
complexity._condition_note: esy/condition.go at 101 is the evaluator's condition kinds: ten kinds, each a small case, plus the qualifier and comparison-set handling the spec describes in §5.1. The per-function maximum is 9 — there is no complex function here, only many simple ones. Splitting the file would scatter the ten kinds that must be read together against the rule syntax.
complexity._expr_note: rulepack/expr.go at 82 is the expression parser: eleven atom kinds and the operator scan that reproduces upstream's detection character for character (ParsingExpertFile.R). Both carry a //nolint with the same reasoning.

function_complexity._default_cap_note: The single most complex function in a file. Unlike the per-file sum, this cannot be satisfied by splitting a file.
function_complexity._parseatom_note: parseAtom at 18: one branch per ESy atom kind, and the syntax has eleven. A dispatch table would move the same eleven cases elsewhere without simplifying anything.
function_complexity._main_note: main.go at 16: flag parsing with flag > environment > default precedence for four options, plus start-up wiring. The composition root is where this belongs.

hotspot._note: A file that is both complex and under-tested fails. Files without coverage data (cmd/habitatus, exercised by the container smoke test rather than by unit tests) are skipped by the script.
